financial_checks.claim: Nikkei fell about 12% on August 5, 2024, the worst day since 1987
financial_checks.result: Closed -12.4% (31,458.42, a 4,451-point fall, the largest ever) per multiple news reports; worst percentage day since -14.9% on Oct 20, 1987. Holds. (secondary reports; not independently confirmed by the reviewer)

financial_checks.claim: Bank of Japan ended yield curve control and raised rates "for the first time in 17 years" in 2024; policy rate "around 1%" in 2026
financial_checks.result: Rate reached 1.0% on June 16, 2026 per news reports, after 0.75% in December 2025; the 2024 end of negative rates and YCC in March is recall. "30-year high" is accurate (highest since 1995). (secondary reports; not independently confirmed by the reviewer)

financial_checks.claim: Japan is the largest foreign holder of US Treasuries; Moody's removed its last AAA in 2025
financial_checks.result: TIC data (June 2026): Japan about $1.117 trillion, first; the Moody's downgrade is recall (May 2025). (secondary reports; not independently confirmed by the reviewer)

financial_checks.claim: Deficit about $1.75 trillion; national debt "blown past 37 trillion"; 30-year Treasury "up around 5%"
financial_checks.result: Deficit figure is in the right range for FY2025; the $37 trillion level is a mid-2025 figure and understates a June 2026 value; the 30-year yield was not checked for June 2026.

financial_checks.claim: US Treasuries paid "four, sometimes 5%" through 30 years of the carry trade
financial_checks.result: Stylised: US yields were at those levels mainly after 2022; currency-hedged returns were small for much of the period.

financial_checks.claim: Yen carry trade size "in the trillions"; Japanese net selling of foreign bonds in 2025; 30- and 40-year JGB record yields; Ray Dalio "debt death spiral"; "trillions of dollars vaporized in about 72 hours"
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified; the carry-trade size is highly estimate-dependent.

strengths: Strong BUT/THEREFORE spine and plain analogies.
Verifiable recent facts (the 2026 rate decision, Nikkei move, TIC ranking).
Self-limiting caveat section ("not here to sell you a panic").
weaknesses: Packaging promises a crash the body argues against.
Conflates leveraged carry trades with institutional bond investing in the John story.
Stale debt figure and a stylised 30-year yield claim.
contradictions: "So boring that financial media cannot turn it into a thumbnail" versus an alarm-style "IT'S HAPPENING AGAIN" thumbnail.
Title and thumbnail imply imminent impact versus "slow leak ... probably the most likely version".
Community pitch says "the rest of the video stands completely on its own" yet sits between the last argument and the recap.
"The Japanese government bonds they're now buying ... those are getting sold off" in one sentence.
improvement_opportunities: Title with the topic and a bounded claim, e.g. "Japan's Bond Market Could Keep Your Mortgage Rate High".
Thumbnail from the script's own imagery (a yen-to-dollar flow arrow, a rate line), not a 2008 reference.
Split the carry-trade unwind (August 2024) from the institutional repatriation argument and state which drives the Treasury demand claim.
Update the debt and yield figures to the upload month and move the community pitch to the end.
unavailable: Treasury and BoJ primary documents (secondary reports used)
